result:
Round 94 is implemented and waiting for C. Nothing was committed or pushed. HEAD is still `85fcb05`, all 518 frozen files are unchanged, and the tree shows exactly 5 modified and 2 new files.

**What changed**
- **Empty collection:** an empty collection now shows a new text for its origin instead of "loading" forever. Demo: `დემო კოლექციაში წყარო არ არის — ბიბლიოთეკა ცარიელია.` Purchased: `შეძენილ კოლექციაში წყარო არ არის — ბიბლიოთეკა ცარიელია.`. No source loading is attempted.
- **Collection change:** the status now goes back to the new collection's loading text, so the old "ready" text no longer lingers. The edit is confined to the load effect in `ArrangementContext.tsx`, plus the new `empty` field in `collection.ts`.
- **Mount safety:** before editing I checked that nothing sets the status during mount. No provider effect does, no child component's mount effect does, `/studio-lab` doesn't, and there's no `StrictMode`. The code-reviewer reached the same conclusion.
- **Tests:** PC9 in `collection.test.ts` only gained the two `empty` keys. The new `collection-load-status.test.tsx` has 10 tests: LS1–LS7, PM1, plus LS3b, which I added after review.
- **Docs:** status line in doc 081, one line in `arrangement-workspace.md`, and the new doc 082.

**Checks run**
- **Before the fix (B's original code in a scratch copy):** 7 tests fail (LS1, LS2, LS3, LS3b, both LS4 cases, LS5) and 3 pass (LS6, LS7, PM1).
  - B expected LS4 to pass on the old code. But B's own LS4 spec requires the purchased loading text right after the switch, which the old code can't produce, so it fails on exactly that line. The part of LS4 that checks old results are ignored is proven by mutation e instead.
- **Mutations a–f:** each turns at least one test red, matching B's table. The unmodified scratch copy passes 41/41.
- **Static checks:** typecheck, lint and Biome on my four code files all pass with no diagnostics; formatting matches.
- **Targeted tests:** 39 files, 716 tests, all pass.
- **My own browser check** (not C evidence), 1440×900 on `/studio-lab`:
  - the server-rendered page shows the demo loading text, and it stays there while the audio is held, then switches to the exact ready text;
  - each audio file is requested once, and there are no hydration warnings or console errors;
  - no token, R2 or other blocked requests, and no `Authorization` headers.
- I did not run the full suite, build or `npm run verify`; those are root gate rows.

**Code review:** the code-reviewer agent scored it 8/10 with no Critical or High findings.
- **Fixed:**
  - Medium: I added LS3b, which switches to a new collection object with the same origin.
  - LS4 no longer pins the old source's state at "loading".
  - The LS7 title is clearer.
  - The wording in `arrangement-workspace.md` line 44 is fixed.
- **Not fixed, outside my grant:**
  - Line 45 of that doc still links to doc 080, not 082.
  - When the collection changes, the old sources' states, buffers and waveforms are never cleared. That was already the case before this round; I suggest a backlog item before the purchased Studio is mounted.

**Architecture note from the reviewer, verbatim:**
> Signal 3 (repeated costly change): the collection-load effect in `app/contexts/ArrangementContext.tsx:3000–3051` has been revisited across rounds 92–94, and each change needs a roughly 300-line copied provider harness to test. Proposal for the planner only: if SRW-21 adds more load or swap rules, consider one bounded task that moves the per-run load bookkeeping (pending/failed counting, choosing the status text) into a pure `lib/arrangement` helper with its own unit tests. The effect, the refs, the abort ownership and the shape of `useArrangement()` would stay unchanged. Until then, keeping it as is is reasonable, because the logic is cohesive and shares one lifecycle.

It's a proposal only; nothing was extracted.

**Open items**
- An empty collection or a collection change can't be reached in the browser on `/studio-lab` until the purchased Studio is mounted, so both fixes are proven by unit tests only.
- The stale `a-browse.json.lock` (its process is gone) is still in place.
- The backlog is not complete.

Files are in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- a-round-94.md
- a-round-94/setup-scratch.sh — rebuilds the scratch copy for C on a fresh machine
